facts.text: The user requested completing only parts c and d of an assignment.
The user asked whether two parties retweet each other at the same rates.
The user asked to calculate retweet counts by each party using a table named "party_cong_retweet_counts".
The user asked to calculate and display the joint probability of party and whether the retweet comes from a MoC in a table named "party_cong_retweet_joint".
The user asked to calculate the conditional probability of retweeting a MoC conditioning on the party.
The user said it was acceptable to use marginal probabilities calculated in Part (a) for the conditional probability.
The user asked which party has the higher conditional probability of retweeting a MoC and why conditional probability was needed instead of joint probabilities.
The user asked that if party and retweeting a MoC are independent in the population described in 1(c), then the joint distribution should be close to the product of marginal probabilities.
The user asked to create expected probabilities under independence in a table named "party_cong_retweet_indep".
The user noted that the function np.outer is useful for creating the independence-expected table.
The user asked to display the independence-expected table and comment if it looks like the joint probability table from 1(c).

keyphrases: independence of party and MoC retweeting
